feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: seasonal ET dynamics are fully simulable in single-column ELM, but automated validation against 'local' eddy-covariance towers is constrained because no AmeriFlux/FLUXNET tower lies inside the Passaic River basin; ELM itself does not ingest or compare against flux-tower observations (that is an external post-processing step).
answerable: Simulate multi-year, monthly-resolved evapotranspiration (latent heat flux and its transpiration/soil-evaporation/canopy-evaporation partitioning) for representative land units of the Passaic basin
Characterize the seasonal cycle, spring green-up onset, and summer peak ET across contrasting soil textures and land cover
Produce ELM ET output at fixed lat/lon points suitable for offline comparison to observations
not_answerable: In-basin eddy-covariance validation: there is no long-record flux tower physically located within the Passaic River basin (nearest NJ AmeriFlux site, US-Slt Silas Little, is in the Pine Barrens ~90 km south, in a different physiography)

ELM/PFLOTRAN cannot perform the observation-model comparison internally; flux-tower matching, footprint gap-filling, and statistical validation are external tasks requiring FLUXNET data not part of these models
Sub-basin routed streamflow or basin-integrated ET requires a distributed/routing configuration, not a single-column setup

parsed.n_justification: Four single columns span the dominant land-surface controls on ET in the Passaic basin: upland deciduous forest on the glaciated Highlands, suburban/mixed lowland on silt loam Piedmont soils, a Great Swamp riparian wetland on organic/clay soils, and a sandy well-drained terrace. This brackets the vegetation and drainage gradients that govern seasonal ET partitioning while keeping the ensemble small and interpretable.
assumptions: GSWP3/CRUNCEP reanalysis forcing is used with a preceding accelerated-decomposition and normal spinup to equilibrate soil moisture and carbon pools before the 20-year analysis window

PFT and soil-texture surface data are taken from default ELM surface datasets at the specified points; suburban column is approximated as a mixed grass/broadleaf-deciduous mosaic since ELM lacks a full urban ET treatment here
Satellite phenology (SP) mode or prognostic BGC can be selected; SP mode is assumed for cleaner LAI-driven seasonal ET characterization

Flux-tower validation is treated as an offline step: ELM ET (EFLX_LH_TOT converted to mm) is exported for comparison to the nearest available AmeriFlux data (e.g., US-Slt) with the explicit caveat that no tower lies within the basin
Single-column runs neglect lateral flow and river routing; basin-scale aggregation would require weighting columns by land-cover area or a spatially distributed configuration
